description: A bass drum: a sine whose pitch and level each fall away from a struck peak, run through a wavefolder and a hard clipper that a separate input can borrow for distortion on its own

params.text: How long the pitch takes to fall from HIGH to LOW, a half-life of 1ms fully left and 0.201 seconds fully right
How long the level takes to fall, a half-life of 1ms fully left and 0.501 seconds fully right
Scales the voltage at the SLIDE input before it is added to the SLIDE knob, inverting it left of centre; at full, 10V covers the knob's whole travel
Scales the voltage at the LIFE input before it is added to the LIFE knob, inverting it left of centre; at full, 10V covers the knob's whole travel
The pitch the sine is struck at, 100Hz to 500Hz
The pitch the sine falls away to and settles at, 0Hz to 100Hz
Scales the voltage at the HIGH input before it shifts the struck pitch, inverting it left of centre; at full the input tracks 1V per octave
Scales the voltage at the LOW input before it shifts the settled pitch, inverting it left of centre; at full the input tracks 1V per octave
Gain into the hard clipper, unity fully left and five times fully right, with everything past full scale flattened off
Gain into the wavefolder, unity fully left and three times fully right; anything driven past full scale is reflected back inside instead of clipping
Scales the voltage at the DIST'R'N input before it is added to the DIST'R'N knob, inverting it left of centre; at full, 10V covers the knob's whole travel
Scales the voltage at the FOLD input before it is added to the FOLD knob, inverting it left of centre; at full, 10V covers the knob's whole travel
How many times the folding stage is run over the wave, a whole number from 1 to 5

inputs.text: Adds to the SLIDE knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's own range
Adds to the LIFE knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's own range
Multiplies the struck pitch by two for every volt, scaled first by the HIGH attenuverter, so it does nothing while that attenuverter is at zero
Multiplies the settled pitch by two for every volt, scaled first by the LOW attenuverter, so it does nothing while that attenuverter is at zero
A rising edge above 1V strikes the drum: the phase restarts, the level jumps to full and the pitch jumps to HIGH
Adds to the DIST'R'N knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's own range
Adds to the FOLD knob through its attenuverter, the total clamped to the knob's own range
Audio for the folder and the clipper on their own, with no envelope and no oscillator, taken one polyphonic channel at a time

outputs.text: The falling pitch envelope, 5V while the sine is at HIGH and 0V once it has reached LOW
The falling level envelope, 5V at the strike and decaying towards 0V
The drum itself, the sine swinging ±5V at the strike, scaled by the level envelope and shaped by the folder and the clipper
The DIST-IN signal after folding and clipping, carrying as many channels as it arrived with

notes: nothing sounds until a trigger arrives at TRIG; on a freshly added module the level has already decayed to silence.
the folder and the clipper are shared: NUMBER, FOLD and DIST'R'N shape the drum and the DIST-IN signal at the same time.
ENV(S) is scaled by the gap between HIGH and LOW; set HIGH to 100Hz and LOW to 100Hz and that jack divides by zero.
